sentences.zh: 徐貞女，宣城人。

translations.literal: Xu the Chaste Woman was a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu the Chaste Woman was from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 少字施之濟。

translations.literal: In her youth she was betrothed to Shi Zhiji.
translations.idiomatic: In her youth she was betrothed to Shi Zhiji.

sentences.zh: 年十五，裏豪湯一泰艷之，倚從子祭酒賓尹，強委禽焉。

translations.literal: At the age of fifteen, a local bully named Tang Yitai lusted after her; relying on his nephew Bin Yin the libationer, he forcibly sent betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen, a local bully named Tang Yitai desired her; relying on his nephew Bin Yin the libationer, he forcibly sent betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 女父子仁不受，夜趣施舁女歸。

translations.literal: The maiden's father Ziren refused to accept them; that night he urged the Shi family to carry his daughter home.
translations.idiomatic: The girl's father Ziren refused; that night he urged the Shi family to carry his daughter home.

sentences.zh: 一泰恚甚，脅有司攝施婦，欲庭奪以歸，先使人捽之濟父子及媒妁數人，毆之府門，有司莫能制。

translations.literal: Yitai was furious; he coerced officials into summoning the Shi woman, intending to seize her publicly in court and take her home. First he sent men to drag the Shi father and son and several matchmakers, beating them at the government gate; the officials could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yitai was furious. He coerced officials into summoning the Shi woman, intending to seize her in open court and take her home. First he sent men to drag off the Shi father and son and several matchmakers, beating them at the government gate, and the officials could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 徐氏被攝，候理，次城東旅舍，思不免，夜伺人靜，投池中死，衣上下縫紉不見寸體。

translations.literal: Lady Xu was summoned and waited for her case at an inn east of the city wall. Thinking she could not escape dishonor, she waited until night when all was quiet, then threw herself into a pool and died; her upper and lower garments were stitched together so that not an inch of flesh showed.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned, Lady Xu waited for her case at an inn east of the city wall. Concluding she could not escape dishonor, she waited until the night was still, then threw herself into a pool and died; her upper and lower garments were stitched together so that not an inch of flesh showed.

sentences.zh: 觀者皆泣下，共舁古廟，盛夏郁蒸，蠅不敢近。

translations.literal: Onlookers all wept; together they carried her to an ancient temple. In the sweltering midsummer heat, flies dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers all wept and together carried her to an ancient temple. In the sweltering midsummer heat, flies dared not approach her body.

sentences.zh: 郡守張德明臨視，立祠城東祀之。

translations.literal: The prefect Zhang Deming came to view her remains and erected a shrine east of the city to sacrifice to her.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Deming came to view her remains and erected a shrine east of the city to honor her.

sentences.zh: 劉氏，京師人。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was a native of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu was from the capital.

sentences.zh: 有松江人戍邊者，詐稱無妻，娶劉。

translations.literal: A man from Songjiang who was on frontier garrison duty falsely claimed to have no wife and married Liu.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Songjiang serving on frontier garrison duty falsely claimed to have no wife and married Liu.

sentences.zh: 既而遇赦歸，紿劉曰：「吾暫歸省。

translations.literal: Later he happened to be pardoned and return home; he deceived Liu, saying, "I am going home briefly to visit my family.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was pardoned and returned home. He deceived Liu, saying, "I am going home briefly to visit my family.

sentences.zh: 」久之不復至，劉抵松訪之，夫拒不納。

translations.literal: " For a long time he did not return; Liu went to Songjiang to seek him out, but her husband refused to take her in.
translations.idiomatic: " For a long time he did not return. Liu went to Songjiang to find him, but her husband refused to take her in.

sentences.zh: 劉哭曰：「良人棄我，我將安歸。

translations.literal: Liu wept and said, "My husband has abandoned me—where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: Liu wept and said, "My husband has abandoned me—where shall I go?

sentences.zh: 」乃剪發為尼，行乞市上，人多憐而周之。

translations.literal: " She then cut her hair and became a nun, begging in the marketplaces; many people pitied her and gave her charity.
translations.idiomatic: " She then cut her hair and became a nun, begging in the marketplaces; many people pitied her and gave her alms.

sentences.zh: 劉置一棺，夜臥棺中數十年。

translations.literal: Liu purchased a coffin and for decades slept in it at night.
translations.idiomatic: Liu bought a coffin and for decades slept in it at night.

sentences.zh: 鄰火起，劉入棺，呼曰：「乞與闔棺，以畢吾事。

translations.literal: When a fire broke out nearby, Liu entered the coffin and called out, "I beg you to close the coffin lid and complete my final rite.
translations.idiomatic: When a fire broke out nearby, Liu entered the coffin and called out, "Please close the coffin lid and complete my final rite.

sentences.zh: 」遂焚死。

translations.literal: " And so she burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: " And so she burned to death.

sentences.zh: 余氏，黃岡宋蒙妾。

translations.literal: Lady Yu was a concubine of Song Meng of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu was a concubine of Song Meng of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 蒙妻劉，舉子女各一人，余無所出。

translations.literal: Meng's wife Liu bore one son and one daughter; Yu had no children of her own.
translations.idiomatic: Meng's wife Liu bore one son and one daughter; Yu had no children of her own.

sentences.zh: 及蒙卒，劉他適，妾辛勤育之。

translations.literal: When Meng died, Liu remarried elsewhere; the concubine toiled to raise the children.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng died, Liu remarried elsewhere, and the concubine toiled to raise the children.

sentences.zh: 日事紡績，非丙夜不休。

translations.literal: Day after day she spun and wove, not resting unless it was after the third watch.
translations.idiomatic: Day after day she spun and wove, not resting until after the third watch.

sentences.zh: 壺政嚴肅，親屬莫敢窺其門。

translations.literal: Her household conduct was stern and proper; relatives dared not peek through her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Her household conduct was stern and proper; relatives dared not peek through her gate.

sentences.zh: 逾二十年，忽謂子女曰：「吾命將盡，不能終視若輩，惟望若輩為上流人爾。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years, she suddenly told the children, "My life is nearly finished; I cannot watch over you to the end. I only hope you will become people of the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: After more than twenty years, she suddenly told the children, "My life is nearly finished; I cannot watch over you to the end. I only hope you will become people of the highest standing.

sentences.zh: 」越數日，無疾而逝。

translations.literal: " Within a few days she passed away without illness.
translations.idiomatic: " Within a few days she passed away without illness.

sentences.zh: 虞鳳娘，義烏人。

translations.literal: Yu Fengniang was a native of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fengniang was from Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 其姊嫁徐明輝而卒，明輝聞鳳娘賢，懇其父欲聘為繼室。

translations.literal: Her elder sister had married Xu Minghui and died; Minghui, hearing Fengniang was virtuous, earnestly asked her father to take her as his second wife.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister had married Xu Minghui and died. Minghui, hearing that Fengniang was virtuous, earnestly asked her father to take her as his second wife.

sentences.zh: 女知，泣謂父母曰：「兄弟未嘗同妻，即姊妹可知。

translations.literal: When the girl learned of this, she wept and told her parents, "Brothers have never shared a wife—from this one can see that sisters should not either.
translations.idiomatic: When the girl learned of this, she wept and told her parents, "Brothers have never shared a wife—so it must be with sisters as well.

sentences.zh: 」父執不聽，女絕口不言，自經死。

translations.literal: " Her father stubbornly refused to listen; the girl said no more and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " Her father stubbornly refused to listen. The girl said no more and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 林貞女，侯官人。

translations.literal: Lin the Chaste Woman was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin the Chaste Woman was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 父舜道，官參政。

translations.literal: Her father Shundao held the post of Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Shundao served as Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 女幼許長樂副都御史陳省子長源，既納幣，長源卒。

translations.literal: In childhood she was betrothed to Changyuan, son of Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Sheng of Changle; after betrothal gifts were exchanged, Changyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood she was betrothed to Changyuan, son of Vice Censor-in-Chief Chen Sheng of Changle. After betrothal gifts were exchanged, Changyuan died.

sentences.zh: 女蓬首削脂澤，稱疾臥床，哭無聲而神傷。

translations.literal: The girl let her hair hang loose, ceased all cosmetics, claimed illness and lay in bed, weeping silently but with spirit deeply wounded.
translations.idiomatic: The girl let her hair hang loose, ceased all cosmetics, claimed illness and lay in bed, weeping silently but with spirit deeply wounded.

sentences.zh: 或謂未成婦，何自苦。

translations.literal: Some said, "You are not yet married—why torment yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "You are not yet married—why torment yourself?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「子名氏、歲月飾而櫝之以歸陳，忍自昧哉！

translations.literal: She replied, "My name and lineage were adorned and packaged to be returned to the Chen family—how could I bear to deny this myself!
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "My name and lineage were adorned and packaged to be returned to the Chen family—how could I bear to deny this myself!

sentences.zh: 」固請於父，欲赴陳喪，父為達其意。

translations.literal: " She repeatedly begged her father to go to the Chen mourning; her father conveyed her wish.
translations.idiomatic: " She repeatedly begged her father to go to the Chen mourning, and her father conveyed her wish.

sentences.zh: 陳父答曰：「以兇歸，所不忍，以好歸，疇與主之？

translations.literal: Chen's father replied, "I cannot bear to receive her in mourning dress; if she comes as a bride, who would receive her?
translations.idiomatic: Chen's father replied, "I cannot bear to receive her in mourning dress. If she comes as a bride, who would receive her?

sentences.zh: 姑俟喪除。

translations.literal: For now let us wait until the mourning period ends.
translations.idiomatic: For now let us wait until the mourning period ends.

sentences.zh: 」女大悲咤曰：「是欲緩之，覬奪吾誌也。

translations.literal: " The girl cried out in great grief, "This is meant to delay me and steal away my resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " The girl cried out in great grief, "This is meant to delay me and steal away my resolve.

sentences.zh: 」遂不食，積七日，嘔血死。

translations.literal: " She then stopped eating; after seven days she vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: " She then stopped eating. After seven days she vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 王貞女，昆山人，太仆卿宇之孫，諸生述之女，字侍郎顧章誌孫同吉。

translations.literal: Wang the Chaste Woman was a native of Kunshan, granddaughter of Grand Master of Stud Wang Yu, daughter of the licentiate Shu; she was betrothed to Tongji, grandson of Vice Minister Gu Zhizhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang the Chaste Woman was from Kunshan, granddaughter of Grand Master of Stud Wang Yu and daughter of the licentiate Shu. She was betrothed to Tongji, grandson of Vice Minister Gu Zhizhang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，同吉卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Tongji died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Tongji died.

sentences.zh: 女即去飾，白衣至父母前，不言亦不泣，若促駕行者。

translations.literal: The girl at once removed her ornaments, dressed in white, and came before her parents—neither speaking nor weeping, as one urging the carriage to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The girl at once removed her ornaments, dressed in white, and came before her parents—neither speaking nor weeping, as one urging the carriage to depart.

sentences.zh: 父母有難色，使嫗告其舅姑，舅姑掃庭內待之。

translations.literal: Her parents showed reluctance; she had an old woman tell her future parents-in-law, who swept the courtyard to receive her.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents showed reluctance, so she had an old woman tell her future parents-in-law, who swept the courtyard to receive her.

sentences.zh: 女既至，拜柩而不哭，斂容見舅姑，有終焉之意。

translations.literal: When the girl arrived, she bowed before the coffin without weeping, composed herself to greet her parents-in-law, showing the intention to remain there for life.
translations.idiomatic: When the girl arrived, she bowed before the coffin without weeping, composed herself to greet her parents-in-law, showing that she meant to remain there for life.

sentences.zh: 姑含淚曰：「兒不幸早亡，奈何累新婦。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law said through tears, "My son died young by misfortune—how can I burden the new bride?
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law said through tears, "My son died young by misfortune—how can I burden the new bride?

sentences.zh: 」女聞姑稱新婦，淚簌簌下，遂留執婦道不去。

translations.literal: " When the girl heard her mother-in-law call her the new bride, tears streamed down; she stayed and fulfilled the wife's duties without leaving.
translations.idiomatic: " When the girl heard her mother-in-law call her the new bride, tears streamed down, and she stayed to fulfill the wife's duties without leaving.

sentences.zh: 早晚跪奠柩前，視姑眠食外，輒自屏一室，雖至戚遣女奴候視，皆謝絕，曰：「吾義不見門以外人。

translations.literal: Morning and evening she knelt in offering before the coffin; apart from attending to her mother-in-law's sleep and meals, she always secluded herself in one room. Even when close relatives sent maidservants to inquire after her, she declined them all, saying, "By my duty I will not see anyone outside this gate.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening she knelt in offering before the coffin. Apart from attending to her mother-in-law's sleep and meals, she always secluded herself in one room. Even when close relatives sent maidservants to inquire after her, she declined them all, saying, "By my duty I will not see anyone outside this gate.

sentences.zh: 」後姑病，女服勤，晝夜不懈。

translations.literal: " Later when her mother-in-law fell ill, the girl served her diligently, day and night without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: " Later when her mother-in-law fell ill, the girl served her diligently, day and night without slackening.

sentences.zh: 及病劇，女人候床前，出視藥竈，往來再三，若有所為。

translations.literal: When the illness grew severe, the girl waited at the bedside, then went out to look at the medicine stove, going back and forth several times as if doing something.
translations.idiomatic: When the illness grew severe, the girl waited at the bedside, then went out to look at the medicine stove, going back and forth several times as if doing something.

sentences.zh: 群婢窺之而莫得其跡，姑既進藥則睡，覺而病立間，呼女曰：「向飲我者何藥？

translations.literal: The maidservants watched but could not discover what she had done; once the mother-in-law had taken the medicine she fell asleep, and when she awoke her illness was immediately relieved. She called to the girl, "What medicine did you give me just now?
translations.idiomatic: The maidservants watched but could not discover what she had done. Once the mother-in-law had taken the medicine she fell asleep, and when she awoke her illness was immediately relieved. She called to the girl, "What medicine did you give me just now?

sentences.zh: 乃速愈如是。

translations.literal: That it should recover so quickly!
translations.idiomatic: That it should recover so quickly!

sentences.zh: 」欲執其手勞之，女縮手有難進之狀。

translations.literal: " She wanted to take her hand to comfort her, but the girl drew back her hand with an air of reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: " She wanted to take her hand to comfort her, but the girl drew back with an air of reluctance.

sentences.zh: 姑怪起視，已斷一指煮藥中矣。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law, puzzled, rose to look and found that she had already cut off a finger and boiled it in the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law, puzzled, rose to look and found she had already cut off a finger and boiled it in the medicine.

sentences.zh: 姑嘆曰：「吾以天奪吾子，常憂老無所倚。

translations.literal: Her mother-in-law sighed and said, "Heaven took my son from me, and I always feared growing old with no one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother-in-law sighed and said, "Heaven took my son from me, and I always feared growing old with no one to rely on.

sentences.zh: 今婦不惜支體以療吾疾，豈不勝有子耶！

translations.literal: Now my daughter-in-law spares not her own flesh to cure my illness—is this not better than having a son!
translations.idiomatic: Now my daughter-in-law spares not her own flesh to cure my illness—is this not better than having a son!

sentences.zh: 」流涕久之。

translations.literal: " She wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: " She wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 人皆稱貞孝女雲。

translations.literal: People all called her the chaste and filial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: People all called her the chaste and filial daughter.

sentences.zh: 倪美玉，年十八歸董緒。

translations.literal: Ni Meiyu, at eighteen, married Dong Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Ni Meiyu married Dong Xu at eighteen.

sentences.zh: 緒居喪過毀得疾，謂妻曰：「吾無兄弟，又無子。

translations.literal: Xu, in excessive grief during mourning, fell ill and told his wife, "I have no brothers and no son.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, grieving excessively during mourning, fell ill and told his wife, "I have no brothers and no son.

sentences.zh: 吾死，父母祀絕矣。

translations.literal: When I die, my parents' sacrifices will cease.
translations.idiomatic: When I die, my parents' sacrifices will cease.

sentences.zh: 當以吾屋為小宗祠，置祀田數畝，小宗人遞主之，春秋享祀，吾父母獲與焉，吾無憾矣。

translations.literal: You should use my house as a small ancestral hall, set aside several acres as sacrificial fields, and have members of the minor lineage take turns overseeing them; at spring and autumn offerings my parents will share in them, and I will have no regrets.
translations.idiomatic: Use my house as a small ancestral hall and set aside several acres as sacrificial fields. Let members of the minor lineage take turns overseeing them. At spring and autumn offerings my parents will share in them, and I will have no regrets.

sentences.zh: 汝必以此意告我叔父而行之。

translations.literal: You must tell my uncle this intention and carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: You must tell my uncle this intention and carry it out.

sentences.zh: 」緒卒，倪立從子為後。

translations.literal: " When Xu died, Ni established a nephew as heir.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xu died, Ni established a nephew as heir.

sentences.zh: 治喪畢，攜其女及田二十畝囑其姒曰：「以此累姆。

translations.literal: When the funeral was complete, she brought her daughter and twenty acres of fields and entrusted them to her sister-in-law, saying, "I leave this burden with you.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral was complete, she brought her daughter and twenty acres of fields and entrusted them to her sister-in-law, saying, "I leave this burden with you.

sentences.zh: 」及夫叔父自外郡至，泣拜致夫命，叔父如其言。

translations.literal: " When her husband's uncle arrived from another prefecture, she wept and bowed to convey her husband's final wishes, and the uncle did as instructed.
translations.idiomatic: " When her husband's uncle arrived from another prefecture, she wept and bowed to convey her husband's final wishes, and the uncle did as instructed.

sentences.zh: 事竣，婦出拜謝，即入室臥不食。

translations.literal: When the matter was finished, the wife came out to bow in thanks, then entered her room, lay down, and stopped eating.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was finished, the wife came out to bow in thanks, then entered her room, lay down, and stopped eating.

sentences.zh: 居數日，沐浴整衣曰：「亡夫召我矣。

translations.literal: After several days, she bathed, dressed herself neatly, and said, "My dead husband is calling me.
translations.idiomatic: After several days, she bathed, dressed herself neatly, and said, "My dead husband is calling me.

sentences.zh: 」舉手別父母親屬而逝，年二十二。

translations.literal: " She raised her hand in farewell to parents and relatives and passed away, aged twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: " She raised her hand in farewell to parents and relatives and passed away at twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 劉烈女，錢塘人。

translations.literal: The Fiercely Chaste Woman Liu was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiercely Chaste Woman Liu was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 少字吳嘉諫。

translations.literal: In her youth she was betrothed to Wu Jiajian.
translations.idiomatic: In her youth she was betrothed to Wu Jiajian.

sentences.zh: 鄰富兒張阿官屢窺之，一夕緣梯入。

translations.literal: A rich neighbor's son, Zhang Aguan, repeatedly spied on her; one night he climbed in by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: A rich neighbor's son, Zhang Aguan, repeatedly spied on her. One night he climbed in by ladder.

sentences.zh: 女呼父母共執之，將訟官。

translations.literal: The girl called her parents to seize him together and intended to bring suit before the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: The girl called her parents to seize him together and intended to bring suit before the authorities.

sentences.zh: 張之從子倡言劉女誨淫，縛人取財。

translations.literal: Zhang's nephew spread the claim that the Liu girl had seduced him and bound people to extort money.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's nephew spread the claim that the Liu girl had seduced him and bound people to extort money.

sentences.zh: 人多信之。

translations.literal: Many people believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Many people believed it.

sentences.zh: 女呼告父曰：「賊汙我名，不可活矣，我當訴帝求直耳。

translations.literal: The girl cried out to her father, "The villain has stained my name—I cannot go on living. I shall appeal to Heaven for justice.
translations.idiomatic: The girl cried out to her father, "The villain has stained my name—I cannot go on living. I shall appeal to Heaven for justice.

sentences.zh: 」即自縊。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She then hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 盛暑待驗，暴日下無屍氣。

translations.literal: In the sweltering summer heat while awaiting official inspection, exposed under the blazing sun, there was no odor of decay.
translations.idiomatic: In the sweltering summer heat while awaiting official inspection, exposed under the blazing sun, there was no odor of decay.

sentences.zh: 嘉諫初惑人言，不哭。

translations.literal: At first Jiajian, misled by people's words, did not weep.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jiajian, misled by people's words, did not weep.

sentences.zh: 徐察之，知其誣也，伏屍大慟。

translations.literal: Gradually examining the matter, he learned she had been slandered; he threw himself on the corpse and wailed bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Gradually examining the matter, he learned she had been slandered. He threw himself on the corpse and wailed bitterly.

sentences.zh: 女目忽開，流血淚數行，若對泣者。

translations.literal: The girl's eyes suddenly opened, and several lines of bloody tears flowed, as if weeping face to face with him.
translations.idiomatic: The girl's eyes suddenly opened, and several lines of bloody tears flowed, as if weeping face to face with him.

sentences.zh: 張延訟師丁二執前說，女傅魂於二曰：「若以筆汙我，我先殺汝。

translations.literal: Zhang retained the litigator Ding Er to maintain the earlier claim; the girl's spirit possessed Er and said, "If you stain me with your pen, I will kill you first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang retained the litigator Ding Er to maintain the earlier claim. The girl's spirit possessed Er and said, "If you stain me with your pen, I will kill you first.

sentences.zh: 」二立死。

translations.literal: " Er died on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: " Er died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時江濤震吼，岸土裂崩數十丈，人以為女冤所致。

translations.literal: At that time the river surged with roaring waves, and the riverbank split and collapsed for dozens of yards; people believed this was caused by the girl's wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the river surged with roaring waves, and the riverbank split and collapsed for dozens of yards. People believed this was caused by the girl's wrongful death.

sentences.zh: 有司遂杖殺阿官及從子。

translations.literal: The authorities then had Aguan and his nephew beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities then had Aguan and his nephew beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 上海某氏，既嫁，夫患瘋癩，舅姑謀奪以妻少子。

translations.literal: A woman of Shanghai (surname withheld), after marrying, found her husband afflicted with leprosy; her parents-in-law plotted to take her away and marry her to their younger son.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of Shanghai (surname withheld), after marrying, found her husband afflicted with leprosy. Her parents-in-law plotted to take her away and marry her to their younger son.

sentences.zh: 婦覺，密告其夫，夫泣遣之歸寧。

translations.literal: The wife discovered this and secretly told her husband; he wept and sent her back to her parents' home.
translations.idiomatic: The wife discovered this and secretly told her husband. He wept and sent her back to her parents' home.

sentences.zh: 婦潛制殮具，夫既死，舅姑不以告，不闔棺，露置水濱，以俗忌惡疾也。

translations.literal: The wife secretly prepared burial goods. When her husband died, her parents-in-law did not inform her, did not close the coffin, and left it exposed by the water's edge, because custom abhorred the foul disease.
translations.idiomatic: The wife secretly prepared burial goods. When her husband died, her parents-in-law did not inform her, did not close the coffin, and left it exposed by the water's edge, because custom abhorred the foul disease.

sentences.zh: 婦聞，盂飯淪雞，偕幼妹至棺所，抱屍浴之，斂以衣衾，闔棺設祭。

translations.literal: When the wife heard of it, she prepared rice in a bowl and stewed chicken, went with her young sister to the coffin, embraced the corpse and bathed it, enshrouded it in garments and quilts, closed the coffin, and set out offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When the wife heard of it, she prepared rice in a bowl and stewed chicken, went with her young sister to the coffin, embraced the corpse and bathed it, enshrouded it in garments and quilts, closed the coffin, and set out offerings.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，與妹訣，以巾幕面，投水死。

translations.literal: When the offerings were complete, she took leave of her sister, veiled her face with a cloth, and drowned herself.
translations.idiomatic: When the offerings were complete, she took leave of her sister, veiled her face with a cloth, and drowned herself.

sentences.zh: 谷氏，余姚史茂妻。

translations.literal: Lady Gu was the wife of Shi Mao of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gu was the wife of Shi Mao of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 父以茂有文學，贅之於家。

translations.literal: Her father, because Mao was learned in letters, took him into the household as a live-in son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Her father, because Mao was learned in letters, took him into the household as a live-in son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 數日，鄰人宋思徵責於父，見氏美，遂指逋錢為聘物，訟之官。

translations.literal: A few days later, a neighbor named Song Sizheng, to whom her father owed money, saw that Lady Gu was beautiful and claimed the debt as betrothal payment, bringing suit before the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later, a neighbor named Song Sizheng, to whom her father owed money, saw that Lady Gu was beautiful and claimed the debt as betrothal payment, bringing suit before the authorities.

sentences.zh: 知縣馬從龍察其誣，杖遣之。

translations.literal: The magistrate Ma Conglong saw through the false claim and had him beaten and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Ma Conglong saw through the false claim and had him beaten and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 及谷下階，茂將扶以行。

translations.literal: As Lady Gu came down the steps, Mao was about to support her as she walked.
translations.idiomatic: As Lady Gu came down the steps, Mao was about to support her as she walked.

sentences.zh: 谷故未嘗出閨閣，見隸人林立，而夫以身近己，慚發赪，推茂遠之。

translations.literal: Lady Gu had never before left the inner quarters; seeing runners standing in ranks and her husband drawing close to her, she flushed with shame and pushed Mao away.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gu had never before left the inner quarters. Seeing runners standing in ranks and her husband drawing close to her, she flushed with shame and pushed Mao away.

sentences.zh: 從龍望見，以谷意不屬茂也，立改判歸思。

translations.literal: Conglong saw this from afar and, thinking Lady Gu's heart did not belong to Mao, immediately reversed the judgment and awarded her to Si.
translations.idiomatic: Conglong saw this from afar and, thinking Lady Gu's heart did not belong to Mao, immediately reversed the judgment and awarded her to Si.

sentences.zh: 思即率眾擁輿中而去，谷母隨之至思舍。

translations.literal: Si at once led a crowd to carry her off in a sedan chair; Lady Gu's mother followed to Si's house.
translations.idiomatic: Si at once led a crowd to carry her off in a sedan chair. Lady Gu's mother followed to Si's house.

sentences.zh: 谷呼號求速死，斷發屬母遺茂。

translations.literal: Lady Gu cried out, begging for a quick death; she cut off her hair, entrusted part to her mother, and sent part to Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gu cried out, begging for a quick death. She cut off her hair, entrusted part to her mother, and sent part to Mao.

sentences.zh: 思族婦十余人，環相勸尉，不可解，乘間縊死。

translations.literal: More than ten women of Si's clan gathered around to counsel and comfort her, but she could not be consoled; seizing an opportunity, she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten women of Si's clan gathered around to counsel and comfort her, but she could not be consoled. Seizing an opportunity, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 從龍聞之大驚，捕思，思亡去。

translations.literal: Conglong was greatly shocked when he heard of it and sought to arrest Si, but Si fled.
translations.idiomatic: Conglong was greatly shocked when he heard of it and sought to arrest Si, but Si fled.

sentences.zh: 茂感妻義，終身不娶。

translations.literal: Mao, moved by his wife's righteousness, never remarried for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Mao, moved by his wife's righteousness, never remarried for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 白氏，清澗惠道昌妻。

translations.literal: Lady Bai was the wife of Hui Daochang of Qingjian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Bai was the wife of Hui Daochang of Qingjian.

sentences.zh: 年十八，夫亡。

translations.literal: At eighteen, her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen, her husband died.

sentences.zh: 懷娠六月，欲以死殉。

translations.literal: Six months pregnant, she wished to die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Six months pregnant, she wished to die with him.

sentences.zh: 眾諭之曰：「胡不少待，舉子以延夫嗣。

translations.literal: Everyone admonished her, saying, "Why not wait a little, bear the child, and continue your husband's line?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone admonished her, saying, "Why not wait a little, bear the child, and continue your husband's line?

sentences.zh: 」氏泣曰：「非不念良人無後，但心痛不能須臾緩耳。

translations.literal: " Lady Bai wept and said, "It is not that I do not think of my husband having no heir, but my heart's pain cannot be eased even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Bai wept and said, "It is not that I do not think of my husband having no heir, but my heart's pain cannot be eased even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 」七日不食而死。

translations.literal: " After seven days without food she died.
translations.idiomatic: " After seven days without food she died.

sentences.zh: 高烈婦，博平諸生賈垓妻。

translations.literal: The Fiercely Chaste Wife Gao was the wife of the licentiate Jia Gai of Boping.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiercely Chaste Wife Gao was the wife of the licentiate Jia Gai of Boping.

sentences.zh: 垓卒，氏自計曰：「死節易，守節難。

translations.literal: When Gai died, Lady Gao reckoned to herself, "Dying for chastity is easy; preserving chastity is hard.
translations.idiomatic: When Gai died, Lady Gao reckoned to herself, "Dying for chastity is easy; preserving chastity is hard.

sentences.zh: 況當兵亂之際，吾寧為其易者。

translations.literal: Moreover, in this time of military turmoil, I would rather choose the easier course.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in this time of military turmoil, I would rather choose the easier course.

sentences.zh: 」執姑手泣曰：「婦不能奉事舅姑，反遺孤孫為累。

translations.literal: " She took her mother-in-law's hand and wept, saying, "Your daughter-in-law cannot serve her parents-in-law and instead leaves an orphaned grandson as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: " She took her mother-in-law's hand and wept, saying, "Your daughter-in-law cannot serve her parents-in-law and instead leaves an orphaned grandson as a burden.

sentences.zh: 然婦殉夫為得正，勿過痛也。

translations.literal: Yet a wife who dies with her husband acts rightly—do not grieve too deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a wife who dies with her husband acts rightly—do not grieve too deeply.

sentences.zh: 」遂縊。

translations.literal: " She then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She then hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 於氏，潁州鄧任妻。

translations.literal: Lady Yu was the wife of Deng Ren of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu was the wife of Deng Ren of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 任病，家貧，藥餌不給，氏罄嫁笥救之。

translations.literal: Ren fell ill; the family was poor and could not afford medicine, so Lady Yu emptied her dowry chest to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren fell ill. The family was poor and could not afford medicine, so Lady Yu emptied her dowry chest to save him.

sentences.zh: 閱六月病革，氏聘簪二，綰一於夫發，自綰其一，撫任頸哽咽曰：「妾必不負君。

translations.literal: After six months his illness became critical; Lady Yu had two hairpins made, fastened one in her husband's hair and one in her own, stroked Ren's neck, and said through sobs, "Your wife will surely not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: After six months his illness became critical. Lady Yu had two hairpins made, fastened one in her husband's hair and one in her own, stroked Ren's neck, and said through sobs, "Your wife will surely not fail you.

sentences.zh: 」納指任口中，令嚙為信。

translations.literal: " She put her finger in Ren's mouth and had him bite it as a pledge.
translations.idiomatic: " She put her finger in Ren's mouth and had him bite it as a pledge.

sentences.zh: 任歿三日，縊死。

translations.literal: Three days after Ren's death, she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Ren's death, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 州又有臺氏，諸生張雲鵬妻。

translations.literal: In the same prefecture there was also Lady Tai, wife of the licentiate Zhang Yunpeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the same prefecture there was also Lady Tai, wife of the licentiate Zhang Yunpeng.

sentences.zh: 夫病，氏單衣蔬食，禱天願代，割臂為糜以進。

translations.literal: When her husband fell ill, Lady Tai wore plain clothes and ate simple food, prayed to Heaven to take his place, cut her arm and made it into a gruel to offer him.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband fell ill, Lady Tai wore plain clothes and ate simple food, prayed to Heaven to take his place, cut her arm and made it into a gruel to offer him.

sentences.zh: 夫病危，許以身殉，訂期三日。

translations.literal: When her husband's illness became critical, she vowed to die with him and set a date three days hence.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband's illness became critical, she vowed to die with him and set a date three days hence.

sentences.zh: 夫付紅帨為訣，氏號泣受之。

translations.literal: Her husband gave her a red scarf as a parting token, and she received it with wailing sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband gave her a red scarf as a parting token, and she received it with wailing sobs.

sentences.zh: 越三日，結所授帨就縊，侍婢救不死，恨曰：「何物奴，敗我事！

translations.literal: Three days later she tied the scarf he had given her and attempted to hang herself; a maidservant saved her, but she hated it and said, "What sort of slave ruins my affair!
translations.idiomatic: Three days later she tied the scarf he had given her and attempted to hang herself. A maidservant saved her, but she hated it and said, "What sort of slave ruins my affair!

sentences.zh: 令我負三日約。

translations.literal: You make me break my three-day pledge.
translations.idiomatic: You make me break my three-day pledge.

sentences.zh: 」自是，水漿不入口，舉聲一號，熱血迸流。

translations.literal: " From then on she took neither water nor food; with each cry, hot blood burst forth.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on she took neither water nor food. With each cry, hot blood burst forth.

sentences.zh: 至七日，頓足曰：「遲矣，郎得毋疑我。

translations.literal: On the seventh day she stamped her foot and said, "It is too late—my husband must not doubt me.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day she stamped her foot and said, "It is too late—my husband must not doubt me.

sentences.zh: 」母偶出櫛沐，扃戶縊死。

translations.literal: " When her mother happened to go out to comb her hair and bathe, she bolted the door and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " When her mother happened to go out to comb her hair and bathe, she bolted the door and hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 胡氏，諸城人，遂平知縣麗明孫女也。

translations.literal: Lady Hu was a native of Zhucheng and granddaughter of Liming, magistrate of Suiping.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu was from Zhucheng and granddaughter of Liming, magistrate of Suiping.

sentences.zh: 年十七，歸諸生李敬中，生一女而夫卒。

translations.literal: At seventeen she married the licentiate Li Jingzhong, bore one daughter, and then her husband died.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen she married the licentiate Li Jingzhong, bore one daughter, and then her husband died.

sentences.zh: 初哭踴甚哀，比三日不哭，盥櫛拜舅姑堂下，家人怪之，從容答曰：「婦不幸失所天，無子，將從死者地下，不得復事舅姑，幸強飯自愛。

translations.literal: At first she wept and stamped in deep grief; by the third day she no longer wept, but washed, combed her hair, and bowed to her parents-in-law in the hall. The family found this strange; she calmly replied, "Your daughter-in-law has unhappily lost her heaven; she has no son and will follow the dead beneath the earth, and can no longer serve her parents-in-law. I hope you will eat well and take care of yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: At first she wept and stamped in deep grief. By the third day she no longer wept, but washed, combed her hair, and bowed to her parents-in-law in the hall. The family found this strange. She calmly replied, "Your daughter-in-law has unhappily lost her heaven. She has no son and will follow the dead beneath the earth, and can no longer serve her parents-in-law. I hope you will eat well and take care of yourselves.

sentences.zh: 他日叔有子，為亡人立嗣，歲時奠麥飯足矣。

translations.literal: If in the future my husband's younger brother has a son, establish an heir for the deceased; wheat offerings at the seasonal rites will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If in the future my husband's younger brother has a son, establish an heir for the deceased. Wheat offerings at the seasonal rites will suffice.

sentences.zh: 」姑及其母泣止之，不可，乃焚香告柩前，顧家人曰：「洗含汝等親之，不可近男子。

translations.literal: " Her mother-in-law and her own mother wept and tried to stop her, but she would not be dissuaded. She burned incense before the coffin and told the household, "When you wash and dress the body, you are his kin—do not let men come near.
translations.idiomatic: " Her mother-in-law and her own mother wept and tried to stop her, but she would not be dissuaded. She burned incense before the coffin and told the household, "When you wash and dress the body, you are his kin—do not let men come near.

sentences.zh: 」遂入戶自經，母與姑槌門痛哭疾呼，終不顧而死。

translations.literal: " She then entered her room and hanged herself; her mother and mother-in-law beat on the door, weeping and calling urgently, but she paid no heed and died.
translations.idiomatic: " She then entered her room and hanged herself. Her mother and mother-in-law beat on the door, weeping and calling urgently, but she paid no heed and died.

sentences.zh: 王氏，淄川成象妻。

translations.literal: Lady Wang was the wife of Cheng Xiang of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was the wife of Cheng Xiang of Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 夫死，痛哭三日，唇焦齒黑。

translations.literal: When her husband died, she wept bitterly for three days until her lips were parched and her teeth blackened.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband died, she wept bitterly for three days until her lips were parched and her teeth blackened.

sentences.zh: 父不忍，予之水，謝勿飲。

translations.literal: Her father could not bear it and gave her water; she declined and would not drink.
translations.idiomatic: Her father could not bear it and gave her water. She declined and would not drink.

sentences.zh: 又三日，氣息漸微，強起語父曰：「翁姑未葬，夫亦露殯，奈何？

translations.literal: After three more days her breath grew faint; forcing herself up, she told her father, "My parents-in-law are not yet buried, and my husband lies in an exposed coffin—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: After three more days her breath grew faint. Forcing herself up, she told her father, "My parents-in-law are not yet buried, and my husband lies in an exposed coffin—what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 」父許任其事，氏就枕叩頭而瞑，年十七。

translations.literal: " Her father promised to take charge of the matter; Lady Wang lay back on her pillow, knocked her head in thanks, and closed her eyes, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: " Her father promised to take charge of the matter. Lady Wang lay back on her pillow, knocked her head in thanks, and closed her eyes at seventeen.

sentences.zh: 劉孝女，京師人。

translations.literal: The Filial Daughter Liu was a native of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Filial Daughter Liu was from the capital.

sentences.zh: 父蘭卒，矢誌不嫁，以養其母。

translations.literal: When her father Lan died, she vowed never to marry and supported her mother.
translations.idiomatic: When her father Lan died, she vowed never to marry and supported her mother.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，年四十六矣，母病歿，女遂絕粒殉之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, when she was forty-six, her mother fell ill and died; the daughter then stopped eating and died with her.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen, when she was forty-six, her mother fell ill and died. The daughter then stopped eating and died with her.

sentences.zh: 崔氏，香河王錫田妻。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was the wife of Wang Xitian of Xianghe.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was the wife of Wang Xitian of Xianghe.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，城破，氏與眾訣曰：「我義不受辱。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, when the city fell, Lady Cui took leave of everyone and said, "By my duty I will not accept disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen, when the city fell, Lady Cui took leave of everyone and said, "By my duty I will not accept disgrace.

sentences.zh: 」涕泣乳其女，將自縊，家人力持不得遂。

translations.literal: " Weeping, she nursed her daughter and was about to hang herself, but her family forcibly held her back and she could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: " Weeping, she nursed her daughter and was about to hang herself, but her family forcibly held her back and she could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 兵及門，眾俱奔，氏倉皇縊於戶後，恐賊見其貌，或解之也。

translations.literal: When soldiers reached the gate, everyone fled; Lady Cui hastily hanged herself behind the door, fearing that if bandits saw her face they might cut her down.
translations.idiomatic: When soldiers reached the gate, everyone fled. Lady Cui hastily hanged herself behind the door, fearing that if bandits saw her face they might cut her down.

sentences.zh: 高陵李氏，鎮撫劉光燦妻。

translations.literal: Lady Li of Gaoling was the wife of Liu Guangcan, a garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Gaoling was the wife of Liu Guangcan, a garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 夫歿，勵誌苦守。

translations.literal: After her husband's death, she resolved herself to preserve chastity through hardship.
translations.idiomatic: After her husband's death, she resolved herself to preserve chastity through hardship.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，賊陷高陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, bandits captured Gaoling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, bandits captured Gaoling.

sentences.zh: 年七十九，其家掖之走，曰：「未亡人棄先夫室何往？

translations.literal: At seventy-nine, her family supported her as they fled; she said, "Where would a woman who has not yet died abandon her late husband's home to go?
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-nine, her family supported her as they fled. She said, "Where would a woman who has not yet died abandon her late husband's home to go?

sentences.zh: 」語未已，賊露刃入。

translations.literal: " Before she had finished speaking, bandits entered with naked blades.
translations.idiomatic: " Before she had finished speaking, bandits entered with naked blades.

sentences.zh: 即取刀自刺，流血淋漓。

translations.literal: She at once took a knife and stabbed herself; blood poured forth.
translations.idiomatic: She at once took a knife and stabbed herself, blood pouring forth.

sentences.zh: 賊壯其烈，與飲食，怒不受，以碗擊賊，罵曰：「吾忍死四十九年，今啜賊食耶！

translations.literal: The bandits admired her fierceness and offered her food and drink; angrily she refused, struck a bandit with a bowl, and cursed, "I have endured living for forty-nine years—would I now sip food from bandits!
translations.idiomatic: The bandits admired her fierceness and offered her food and drink. Angrily she refused, struck a bandit with a bowl, and cursed, "I have endured living for forty-nine years—would I now sip food from bandits!

sentences.zh: 」遂遇害。

translations.literal: " She was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: " She was then killed.

sentences.zh: 烈婦柴氏，夏縣孫貞妻。

translations.literal: The Fiercely Chaste Wife Chai was the wife of Sun Zhen of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: The Fiercely Chaste Wife Chai was the wife of Sun Zhen of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，夫婦避賊山中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, husband and wife fled bandits into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen, husband and wife fled bandits into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 賊搜山，見氏悅之，執其手。

translations.literal: Bandits searched the mountains, saw Lady Chai and took a liking to her, and seized her hand.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits searched the mountains, saw Lady Chai and took a liking to her, and seized her hand.

sentences.zh: 氏以口嚙肉棄之曰：「賊汙吾手。

translations.literal: Lady Chai bit the flesh from her hand with her mouth and cast it away, saying, "Bandits have stained my hand.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chai bit the flesh from her hand with her mouth and cast it away, saying, "Bandits have stained my hand.

sentences.zh: 」繼扳其肱，又以口嚙肉棄之曰：「賊汙吾肱。

translations.literal: " Then they seized her upper arm; again she bit away the flesh with her mouth and cast it away, saying, "Bandits have stained my arm.
translations.idiomatic: " Then they seized her upper arm. Again she bit away the flesh with her mouth and cast it away, saying, "Bandits have stained my arm.

sentences.zh: 」賊舍之去，氏罵不絕聲，還殺之。

translations.literal: " The bandits let her go, but she cursed without cease, so they returned and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits let her go, but she cursed without cease, so they returned and killed her.

sentences.zh: 周氏，新城王永命妻，登州都督遇吉兄女也。

translations.literal: Lady Zhou was the wife of Wang Yongming of Xincheng and daughter of the elder brother of Yuji, garrison commander of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhou was the wife of Wang Yongming of Xincheng and daughter of the elder brother of Yuji, garrison commander of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼通《孝經》、《列女傳》。

translations.literal: From childhood she was versed in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood she was versed in the Classic of Filial Piety and the Biographies of Exemplary Women.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，叛將耿仲明、李九成等據登州反，縱兵淫掠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, the rebel generals Geng Zhongming, Li Jiucheng, and others seized Dengzhou and rebelled, letting their troops rampage in rapine and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, the rebel generals Geng Zhongming, Li Jiucheng, and others seized Dengzhou and rebelled, letting their troops rampage in rapine and plunder.

sentences.zh: 一小校將辱之，氏紿之去，即投繯死。

translations.literal: A junior officer was about to violate her; Lady Zhou deceived him into leaving, then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer was about to violate her. Lady Zhou deceived him into leaving, then hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊至，怒其誑己，支解之。

translations.literal: The next day bandits arrived, enraged that she had deceived them, and dismembered her body.
translations.idiomatic: The next day bandits arrived, enraged that she had deceived them, and dismembered her body.

sentences.zh: 事平，永命偵賊所在，擊斬之，以其首祭墓。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, Yongming tracked down the bandits' whereabouts, struck them down, and sacrificed their heads at her tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was settled, Yongming tracked down the bandits' whereabouts, struck them down, and sacrificed their heads at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 時蓬萊浦延禧妻王氏，年二十，守節撫孤。

translations.literal: At that time Lady Wang, wife of Pu Yanxi of Penglai, was twenty years old, preserving chastity and raising her orphan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lady Wang, wife of Pu Yanxi of Penglai, was twenty years old, preserving chastity and raising her orphan.

sentences.zh: 九成叛，城陷，叔允章至其家，問所向。

translations.literal: When Jiucheng rebelled and the city fell, her uncle Yunzhang came to her home and asked where she intended to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiucheng rebelled and the city fell, her uncle Yunzhang came to her home and asked where she intended to go.

sentences.zh: 答曰：「兒豈向患難中求活。

translations.literal: She replied, "Would your niece seek life amid hardship?
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "Would your niece seek life amid hardship?

sentences.zh: 」時有麻索在床頭，叔以手振之曰：「欲決計於此乎？

translations.literal: " There was a hemp rope at the head of the bed; her uncle shook it with his hand and said, "Do you wish to resolve the matter here?
translations.idiomatic: " There was a hemp rope at the head of the bed. Her uncle shook it with his hand and said, "Do you wish to resolve the matter here?

sentences.zh: 」氏首肯，從容就縊。

translations.literal: " Lady Wang nodded, and calmly hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Wang nodded and calmly hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 荊媧，陜西淳化人，姓高氏。

translations.literal: Jing Wa was a native of Chunhua in Shaanxi, surname Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Wa was from Chunhua in Shaanxi, surname Gao.

sentences.zh: 兄起鳳，邑諸生。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Qifeng was a licentiate of the district.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Qifeng was a licentiate of the district.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，流賊掠繼母秦氏及荊媧去，起鳳馳赴賊營請贖。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits carried off her stepmother Lady Qin and Jing Wa; Qifeng hurried to the bandit camp to ransom them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits carried off her stepmother Lady Qin and Jing Wa. Qifeng hurried to the bandit camp to ransom them.

sentences.zh: 賊索二馬，起鳳傾貲得一馬，予之。

translations.literal: The bandits demanded two horses; Qifeng spent all his wealth to obtain one horse and gave it to them.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits demanded two horses. Qifeng spent all his wealth to obtain one horse and gave it to them.

sentences.zh: 賊止還其母。

translations.literal: The bandits returned only his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits returned only his mother.

sentences.zh: 起鳳與妹訣曰：「我去，汝即死。

translations.literal: Qifeng took leave of his sister, saying, "When I go, you must die.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng took leave of his sister, saying, "When I go, you must die.

sentences.zh: 」賊令勸妹從己，且欲留為書記。

translations.literal: " The bandits ordered him to persuade his sister to submit to them and also wished to keep him as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits ordered him to persuade his sister to submit to them and also wished to keep him as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 起鳳大罵不從，被殺。

translations.literal: Qifeng cursed them bitterly and refused; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng cursed them bitterly and refused. He was killed.

sentences.zh: 百計脅荊媧，大罵求死。

translations.literal: By every means they coerced Jing Wa; she cursed them and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: By every means they coerced Jing Wa. She cursed them and begged for death.

sentences.zh: 賊悅其色，割發裂衣以恐之。

translations.literal: The bandits admired her beauty, cut her hair and tore her clothes to terrify her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits admired her beauty, cut her hair and tore her clothes to terrify her.

sentences.zh: 媧益罵不已，賊乃殺之，年甫十六。

translations.literal: Jing Wa cursed all the more without cease, so the bandits killed her; she was only sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Wa cursed all the more without cease, so the bandits killed her. She was only sixteen.

sentences.zh: 巡按吳甡上其事，兄妹皆旌。

translations.literal: The touring censor Wu Shen memorialized the affair, and both brother and sister were honored.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Wu Shen memorialized the affair, and both brother and sister were honored.

sentences.zh: 陳丹余妻宋氏。

translations.literal: Lady Song, wife of Chen Danyu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Song, wife of Chen Danyu.

sentences.zh: 丹余為鄖陽諸生。

translations.literal: Danyu was a licentiate of Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Danyu was a licentiate of Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年，賊至被掠，並執其女，迫令入空室。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Chongzhen, when bandits arrived she was seized; they also seized her daughter and forced them into an empty room.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Chongzhen, when bandits arrived she was seized. They also seized her daughter and forced them into an empty room.

sentences.zh: 前有古槐，母女抱樹立，罵曰：「吾母子死白日下，豈受汙暗室中。

translations.literal: Before them stood an ancient pagoda tree; mother and daughter embraced the tree and stood, cursing, "We mother and daughter will die in the open daylight—how could we accept defilement in a dark room!
translations.idiomatic: Before them stood an ancient pagoda tree. Mother and daughter embraced the tree and stood, cursing, "We mother and daughter will die in the open daylight—how could we accept defilement in a dark room!

sentences.zh: 」大罵不行。

translations.literal: " They cursed bitterly and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: " They cursed bitterly and would not go.

sentences.zh: 賊斷其手，益大罵，俱被害。

translations.literal: The bandits cut off their hands; they cursed all the more, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits cut off their hands. They cursed all the more, and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 黃日芳妾李氏、陳氏。

translations.literal: The concubines Lady Li and Lady Chen of Huang Rifang.
translations.idiomatic: The concubines Lady Li and Lady Chen of Huang Rifang.

sentences.zh: 日芳知霍丘縣，崇禎八年，賫計簿入郡。

translations.literal: Rifang was magistrate of Huoqiu; in the eighth year of Chongzhen he carried the account books into the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Rifang was magistrate of Huoqiu. In the eighth year of Chongzhen he carried the account books into the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 流賊突至，圍城。

translations.literal: Roving bandits suddenly arrived and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: Roving bandits suddenly arrived and besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 二人相謂曰：「主君未還，城必不守，我兩人獨有一死耳。

translations.literal: The two said to each other, "Our master has not returned; the city surely cannot be held—we two have only death.
translations.idiomatic: The two said to each other, "Our master has not returned; the city surely cannot be held—we two have only death.

sentences.zh: 」密縫內外衣甚固，城陷，南望再拜，攜赴藏天澗死。

translations.literal: " They secretly stitched their inner and outer garments very firmly; when the city fell, they bowed twice toward the south, went together to Cangtian Stream, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " They secretly stitched their inner and outer garments very firmly. When the city fell, they bowed twice toward the south, went together to Cangtian Stream, and died.

sentences.zh: 越三日，日芳至，號哭澗側。

translations.literal: Three days later Rifang arrived and wailed at the stream's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Rifang arrived and wailed at the stream's edge.

sentences.zh: 兩屍應聲浮出，顏色如生，手尚相援。

translations.literal: The two corpses floated up at the sound; their complexions were as in life, and their hands still clasped each other.
translations.idiomatic: The two corpses floated up at the sound. Their complexions were as in life, and their hands still clasped each other.

sentences.zh: 蘄水李氏，諸生何之旦妻。

translations.literal: Lady Li of Qishui was the wife of the licentiate He Zhidan.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li of Qishui was the wife of the licentiate He Zhidan.

sentences.zh: 流賊至蘄，執而逼之去，不從，則眾挾之。

translations.literal: When roving bandits reached Qi, they seized her and forced her to go with them; she refused, so the crowd dragged her along.
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits reached Qi, they seized her and forced her to go with them. She refused, so the crowd dragged her along.

sentences.zh: 李罵益厲，嚙賊求死。

translations.literal: Lady Li cursed all the more fiercely, bit the bandits, and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li cursed all the more fiercely, bit the bandits, and begged for death.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，刺之，創遍體，未嘗有懼色，賊斷其頸死。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and stabbed her; wounds covered her body, yet she never showed fear; the bandits cut through her neck and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were enraged and stabbed her. Wounds covered her body, yet she never showed fear. The bandits cut through her neck and killed her.

sentences.zh: 從婢阿來抱李幼女，守哭。

translations.literal: Her maidservant Alai held Lady Li's young daughter and kept watch, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Her maidservant Alai held Lady Li's young daughter and kept watch, weeping.

sentences.zh: 賊奪女將殺之，不與，伏地以身庇之。

translations.literal: Bandits seized the girl and were about to kill her; Alai would not give her up and lay on the ground, shielding her with her body.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits seized the girl and were about to kill her. Alai would not give her up and lay on the ground, shielding her with her body.

sentences.zh: 刺數十創，婢、女俱死。

translations.literal: They stabbed her dozens of times; both maidservant and girl died.
translations.idiomatic: They stabbed her dozens of times. Both maidservant and girl died.

sentences.zh: 萬氏，和州儒士姚守中妻，泉州知府慶女孫也。

translations.literal: Lady Wan was the wife of the scholar Yao Shouzhong of Hezhou and granddaughter of Qing, prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wan was the wife of the scholar Yao Shouzhong of Hezhou and granddaughter of Qing, prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 生六子，皆有室。

translations.literal: She bore six sons, all of whom had wives.
translations.idiomatic: She bore six sons, all of whom had wives.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年，流賊陷其城，慟哭孀姑前，命諸婦曰：「我等女子也，誓必死節。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chongzhen, when roving bandits captured the city, she wept bitterly before her widowed mother-in-law and ordered the daughters-in-law, "We are women and swear to die for chastity.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chongzhen, when roving bandits captured the city, she wept bitterly before her widowed mother-in-law and ordered the daughters-in-law, "We are women and swear to die for chastity.

sentences.zh: 」諸子環泣，急麾之曰：「汝輩男子，當圖存宗祀，何泣焉？

translations.literal: " The sons wept in a circle around her; she urgently waved them away, saying, "You are men—you should plan to preserve the lineage. Why weep?
translations.idiomatic: " The sons wept in a circle around her. She urgently waved them away, saying, "You are men—you should plan to preserve the lineage. Why weep?

sentences.zh: 」長子承舜泣曰：「兒讀書，惟識忠孝字耳，願為厲鬼殺賊，何忍母獨死。

translations.literal: " The eldest son Chengshun wept and said, "Your son has read books and knows only the words loyalty and filial piety. I wish to become a vengeful ghost and kill bandits—how can I bear to let my mother die alone!
translations.idiomatic: " The eldest son Chengshun wept and said, "Your son has read books and knows only the words loyalty and filial piety. I wish to become a vengeful ghost and kill bandits—how can I bear to let my mother die alone!

sentences.zh: 」遂負母投於塘。

translations.literal: " He then carried his mother on his back and threw themselves into a pond.
translations.idiomatic: " He then carried his mother on his back and threw themselves into a pond.

sentences.zh: 諸婦女孫相隨死者十數人，僅存子希舜，求其屍，其聚塘坳，無一相離者。

translations.literal: More than ten daughters-in-law, women, and grandchildren followed in death; only the son Xishun survived. When he sought their corpses, they were gathered in the hollow of the pond, not one separated from another.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten daughters-in-law, women, and grandchildren followed in death. Only the son Xishun survived. When he sought their corpses, they were gathered in the hollow of the pond, not one separated from another.

sentences.zh: 流賊陷和州，王氏一時五烈婦；

translations.literal: When roving bandits captured Hezhou, there were at one time five fiercely chaste wives of the Wang clan;
translations.idiomatic: When roving bandits captured Hezhou, there were at one time five fiercely chaste wives of the Wang clan:

sentences.zh: 王用賓妻尹氏，用賢妻杜氏，用聘妻魯氏，用極妻戴氏，又王氏良器女，劉臺妻也。

translations.literal: Lady Yin, wife of Wang Yongbin; Lady Du, wife of Wang Yongxian; Lady Lu, wife of Wang Yongpin; Lady Dai, wife of Wang Yongji; and also the daughter of Wang Liangqi of the Wang clan, wife of Liu Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yin, wife of Wang Yongbin; Lady Du, wife of Wang Yongxian; Lady Lu, wife of Wang Yongpin; Lady Dai, wife of Wang Yongji; and also the daughter of Wang Liangqi of the Wang clan, wife of Liu Tai.

sentences.zh: 五人同匿城西別墅，誓偕死。

translations.literal: The five hid together in a villa west of the city and vowed to die together.
translations.idiomatic: The five hid together in a villa west of the city and vowed to die together.

sentences.zh: 及賊登陴，呼聲震地。

translations.literal: When the bandits mounted the battlements, their shouts shook the earth.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits mounted the battlements, their shouts shook the earth.

sentences.zh: 五人相持泣曰：「亟死亟死，毋汙賊刃。

translations.literal: The five embraced one another weeping and said, "Die quickly, die quickly—do not be stained by bandit blades.
translations.idiomatic: The five embraced one another weeping and said, "Die quickly, die quickly—do not be stained by bandit blades.

sentences.zh: 」結繯，繯斷，適用賢所佩劍掛壁上，杜趨拔之，爭磨以剄，次第死。

translations.literal: " They tied nooses, but the ropes broke; by chance Yongxian's sword hung on the wall—Lady Du rushed to draw it, they competed to sharpen it and cut their throats, and died one after another.
translations.idiomatic: " They tied nooses, but the ropes broke. By chance Yongxian's sword hung on the wall—Lady Du rushed to draw it, they competed to sharpen it and cut their throats, and died one after another.

sentences.zh: 州又有女，失其姓，與諸婦共匿明倫堂後。

translations.literal: In the prefecture there was also a girl whose surname is lost; she hid with several other women behind the Hall of Bright Principle.
translations.idiomatic: In the prefecture there was also a girl whose surname is lost. She hid with several other women behind the Hall of Bright Principle.

sentences.zh: 其四人已為賊執，用帛牽之。

translations.literal: Four of them had already been seized by bandits and were being led away with silk cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Four of them had already been seized by bandits and were being led away with silk cloth.

sentences.zh: 獨此女不肯就執，多方迫之不得。

translations.literal: This girl alone refused to submit to capture; they tried every means to force her but could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: This girl alone refused to submit to capture. They tried every means to force her but could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 四婦勸之，泣曰：「我處女也，可同男子去耶？

translations.literal: The four women urged her; weeping, she said, "I am a maiden—can I go off with men?
translations.idiomatic: The four women urged her. Weeping, she said, "I am a maiden—can I go off with men?

sentences.zh: 」以頭搶地。

translations.literal: " She struck her head against the ground.
translations.idiomatic: " She struck her head against the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊搴其足而曳之，女大罵。

translations.literal: Bandits grabbed her feet and dragged her; the girl cursed them bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits grabbed her feet and dragged her. The girl cursed them bitterly.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，一手搴足，以刀從下劈之，體裂為四。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged; with one hand grabbing her foot, they split her body into four parts with a blade from below.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were enraged. With one hand grabbing her foot, they split her body into four parts with a blade from below.

sentences.zh: 陳氏，涇陽王生妻。

translations.literal: Lady Chen was the wife of Wang Sheng of Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen was the wife of Wang Sheng of Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 有子方晬，生疾將死，以遺孩屬陳。

translations.literal: They had a son just past infancy; when Sheng fell gravely ill and was near death, he entrusted the remaining child to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: They had a son just past infancy. When Sheng fell gravely ill and was near death, he entrusted the remaining child to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳曰：「吾當生死以之。

translations.literal: Chen said, "I will live or die with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "I will live or die with him.

sentences.zh: 」流賊至，陳抱子避樓上。

translations.literal: " When roving bandits arrived, Chen took the child in her arms and fled upstairs.
translations.idiomatic: " When roving bandits arrived, Chen took the child in her arms and fled upstairs.

sentences.zh: 賊燒樓，陳從樓檐跳下，不死。

translations.literal: Bandits burned the building; Chen leaped from the eaves and did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits burned the building. Chen leaped from the eaves and did not die.

sentences.zh: 賊視其色麗，挾之馬上，陳躍身墜地者再。

translations.literal: The bandits, seeing her beauty, lifted her onto a horse; Chen twice threw herself off and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits, seeing her beauty, lifted her onto a horse. Chen twice threw herself off and fell to the ground.

sentences.zh: 最後以索縛之，行數里，陳力斷所系索，並鞍墜焉。

translations.literal: Finally they bound her with a rope; after traveling several li, Chen forcibly broke the rope that bound her and fell from the saddle together with it.
translations.idiomatic: Finally they bound her with a rope. After traveling several li, Chen forcibly broke the rope that bound her and fell from the saddle together with it.

sentences.zh: 賊知不可奪，乃殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits knew she could not be taken and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits knew she could not be taken and killed her.

sentences.zh: 賊退，家人收其屍，子呱呱懷中，兩手猶堅抱如故。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the family collected her corpse; the child wailed in her embrace, and both hands still held him firmly as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits withdrew, the family collected her corpse. The child wailed in her embrace, and both hands still held him firmly as before.

sentences.zh: 雞澤二李氏。

translations.literal: The two Ladies Li of Jize.
translations.idiomatic: The two Ladies Li of Jize.

sentences.zh: 一同邑田蘊璽妻。

translations.literal: One was the wife of Tian Yunxi of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: One was the wife of Tian Yunxi of the same district.

sentences.zh: 遇亂，蘊璽兄弟被殺。

translations.literal: During the turmoil, Yunxi and his brothers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil, Yunxi and his brothers were killed.

sentences.zh: 李抱女同姒王抱男而逃。

translations.literal: Lady Li carried her daughter while her sister-in-law Wang carried a boy as they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li carried her daughter while her sister-in-law Wang carried a boy as they fled.

sentences.zh: 王足創難行，令李速去。

translations.literal: Wang's feet were wounded and she could not walk easily; she told Li to flee quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang's feet were wounded and she could not walk easily. She told Li to flee quickly.

sentences.zh: 李曰：「良人兄弟俱死，當存此子以留田氏後。

translations.literal: Li said, "My husband's brothers are all dead—we must preserve this boy to continue the Tian lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Li said, "My husband's brothers are all dead—we must preserve this boy to continue the Tian lineage.

sentences.zh: 」遂棄己女，抱其子赴城，得無恙。

translations.literal: " She then abandoned her own daughter, carried Wang's son to the city, and both came through unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: " She then abandoned her own daughter, carried Wang's son to the city, and both came through unharmed.

sentences.zh: 一嫁曲周郭某。

translations.literal: The other had married a Guo of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The other had married a Guo of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，舉家走匿。

translations.literal: When turmoil struck, the whole family fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: When turmoil struck, the whole family fled and hid.

sentences.zh: 翁姑旋被殺，李攜幼男及夫弟方七歲者共逃，力罷，不能俱全。

translations.literal: Her parents-in-law were soon killed; Lady Li fled carrying her young son and her husband's seven-year-old younger brother, but her strength gave out and she could not save all.
translations.idiomatic: Her parents-in-law were soon killed. Lady Li fled carrying her young son and her husband's seven-year-old younger brother, but her strength gave out and she could not save all.

sentences.zh: 或教之舍叔而抱男，李曰：「翁姑死矣，叔豈再得乎！

translations.literal: Someone advised her to abandon the uncle and carry the boy; Li said, "My parents-in-law are dead—can I ever get my husband's brother back!
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised her to abandon the uncle and carry the boy. Li said, "My parents-in-law are dead—can I ever get my husband's brother back!

sentences.zh: 子雖難舍，然吾夫在外，或未死，尚可期也。

translations.literal: Though it is hard to abandon my son, my husband is away and may not yet be dead—there is still hope.
translations.idiomatic: Though it is hard to abandon my son, my husband is away and may not yet be dead—there is still hope.

sentences.zh: 」竟棄男，負叔而走。

translations.literal: " In the end she abandoned the boy and carried her brother-in-law as she fled.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end she abandoned the boy and carried her brother-in-law as she fled.

sentences.zh: 宋德成妻姜氏，臨清人。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang, wife of Song Decheng, was a native of Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang, wife of Song Decheng, was from Linqing.

sentences.zh: 德成知贊皇縣，寇入署，姜投井。

translations.literal: Decheng was magistrate of Zanhuang; when bandits entered the yamen, Jiang threw herself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: Decheng was magistrate of Zanhuang. When bandits entered the yamen, Jiang threw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 賊出之，逼令食，罵曰：「待官兵剿汝，醢為脯，吾當食之。

translations.literal: Bandits pulled her out and forced her to eat; she cursed, "Wait until government troops exterminate you—I will mince you into jerky and eat you.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits pulled her out and forced her to eat. She cursed, "Wait until government troops exterminate you—I will mince you into jerky and eat you.

sentences.zh: 」以簪自剔一目示賊曰：「吾廢人也，速殺為幸。

translations.literal: " She gouged out one of her own eyes with a hairpin to show the bandits and said, "I am a ruined person—kill me quickly and I will be grateful.
translations.idiomatic: " She gouged out one of her own eyes with a hairpin to show the bandits and said, "I am a ruined person—kill me quickly and I will be grateful.

sentences.zh: 」賊怒殺之。

translations.literal: " The bandits killed her in rage.
translations.idiomatic: " The bandits killed her in rage.

sentences.zh: 六安女，失其姓。

translations.literal: The daughter of Lu'an, her surname lost.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Lu'an, her surname lost.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，流賊入境，見其美，將犯之。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign, when roving bandits entered the district, they saw her beauty and were about to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, when roving bandits entered the district, they saw her beauty and were about to violate her.

sentences.zh: 以帕蒙其頭，輒壞之，曰：「毋汙我發。

translations.literal: They covered her head with a cloth, but she kept tearing it off, saying, "Do not defile my hair.
translations.idiomatic: They covered her head with a cloth, but she kept tearing it off and said, "Do not defile my hair.

sentences.zh: 」被以錦衣，又擲之曰：「毋汙吾身。

translations.literal: " They dressed her in brocade robes; she threw them off again, saying, "Do not defile my body.
translations.idiomatic: " They dressed her in brocade robes. She threw them off again and said, "Do not defile my body.

sentences.zh: 」強擁諸馬上，復投地大罵請死。

translations.literal: " They forcibly lifted her onto a horse; she threw herself to the ground again, cursing loudly and begging to die.
translations.idiomatic: " They forcibly lifted her onto a horse. She threw herself to the ground again, cursing loudly and begging to die.

sentences.zh: 賊怒刃之，既而嘆曰：「真烈女。」

translations.literal: The bandits killed her in rage with a blade, then sighed and said, "A truly chaste woman."
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed her in a rage. Then they sighed and said, "A truly chaste woman."

sentences.zh: 石氏女，失其邑裏，隨父守仁寓五河。

translations.literal: The daughter of the Shi clan, her native district lost, followed her father Shouren to lodge at Wuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of the Shi clan, her native district unknown, followed her father Shouren to lodge at Wuhe.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，流賊突至，執欲汙之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen, roving bandits suddenly arrived, seized her, and intended to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Chongzhen reign, roving bandits suddenly arrived, seized her, and intended to violate her.

sentences.zh: 女抱槐樹厲聲罵賊。

translations.literal: The girl embraced a locust tree and cursed the bandits in a fierce voice.
translations.idiomatic: The girl clung to a locust tree and cursed the bandits at the top of her voice.

sentences.zh: 賊使數人牽之不解，斫其兩手，罵如初。

translations.literal: The bandits sent several men to pull her but could not loosen her grip; they hacked off both her hands, yet she cursed as before.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits sent several men to pull her, but they could not loosen her grip. They hacked off both her hands, yet she cursed as before.

sentences.zh: 又斷其足，愈罵不絕，痛仆地佯死。

translations.literal: They then severed her feet; she cursed all the more without cease, then collapsed in pain to the ground and feigned death.
translations.idiomatic: They then severed her feet. She cursed all the more without cease, then collapsed in pain and feigned death on the ground.

sentences.zh: 賊就褫其衣，女以口嚙賊指，斷其三，含血升許噴賊，乃瞑。

translations.literal: As the bandits came to strip off her clothes, the girl bit a bandit's finger with her mouth and severed three of them; she held about a sheng of blood in her mouth and sprayed it at the bandits, then closed her eyes.
translations.idiomatic: As the bandits came to strip off her clothes, the girl bit a bandit's finger and severed three of them. She held roughly a sheng of blood in her mouth, sprayed it at the bandits, and then closed her eyes.

sentences.zh: 賊擁薪焚之，厥後所焚地，血痕耿耿，遇雨則燥，旸則濕。

translations.literal: The bandits heaped firewood and burned her; thereafter at the place of burning the bloodstains remained bright—when it rained they were dry, when the sun shone they were wet.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits heaped firewood and burned her. Thereafter at the place of the burning the bloodstains remained vivid: when it rained they were dry, and when the sun shone they were wet.

sentences.zh: 村人駭異，掘去之，色亦入土三尺許。

translations.literal: Villagers were appalled; they dug up the soil and removed it, yet the color had also penetrated about three chi into the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers were appalled. They dug up the soil and removed it, but the color had also seeped about three chi into the earth.

sentences.zh: 又當塗舉人吳昌祚妻謝氏，為亂卒所掠。

translations.literal: Also Lady Xie, wife of the Dangtu licentiate Wu Changzuo, was seized by disorderly soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Lady Xie, wife of the Dangtu licentiate Wu Changzuo, who was seized by disorderly soldiers.

sentences.zh: 謝以手抱樹，大罵不止。

translations.literal: Xie embraced a tree with her hands and cursed loudly without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Xie clung to a tree with her hands and cursed loudly without stopping.

sentences.zh: 卒怒，斷其附樹之指，復拾斷指擲卒面，卒磔殺之。

translations.literal: The soldiers were enraged, cut off the fingers with which she clung to the tree, yet she picked up the severed fingers and threw them in the soldiers' faces; the soldiers dismembered and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers were enraged and cut off the fingers with which she clung to the tree. She picked up the severed fingers and threw them in the soldiers' faces. The soldiers dismembered and killed her.

sentences.zh: 周彥敬妻莊氏。

translations.literal: Zhuang, wife of Zhou Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhuang, wife of Zhou Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 彥敬，棲霞知縣。

translations.literal: Yanjing was magistrate of Qixia.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing was magistrate of Qixia.

sentences.zh: 氏讀書知大義，亂起，鄉人悉竄山穴中。

translations.literal: The lady had read books and understood great principle; when disorder arose, all the villagers fled into mountain caves.
translations.idiomatic: She had studied and understood the greater moral principles. When disorder broke out, all the villagers fled into mountain caves.

sentences.zh: 莊以男女無別，有難色。

translations.literal: Zhuang, because men and women would not be separated, showed reluctance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang hesitated, for men and women would not be kept apart.

sentences.zh: 彥敬強之曰：「不入，且見殺。

translations.literal: Yanjing pressed her, saying, "If you do not enter, you will soon be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjing pressed her and said, "If you do not go in, you will soon be killed.

sentences.zh: 」莊曰：「無禮不如死，君疑我難死乎！

translations.literal: " Zhuang said, "To live without propriety is worse than death—do you doubt that I find death hard?
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuang said, "To live without propriety is worse than death. Do you doubt that I find death hard?

sentences.zh: 」既引刀自裁。

translations.literal: " She then drew a knife and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She then drew a knife and killed herself.

sentences.zh: 彥敬感其義，終身不復娶。

translations.literal: Yanjing was moved by her righteousness and never took another wife for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by her righteousness, Yanjing never took another wife for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 梁凝禧妻馮氏。

translations.literal: Feng, wife of Liang Ningxi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Feng, wife of Liang Ningxi.

sentences.zh: 凝禧，隨州諸生。

translations.literal: Ningxi was a student of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxi was a licentiate of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十年，聞賊警，夫婦買舟避難。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Chongzhen, hearing a bandit alarm, husband and wife bought a boat to flee to safety.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Chongzhen reign, hearing a bandit alarm, the couple bought a boat to flee.

sentences.zh: 行至西河，賊追急，登岸奔魏家砦。

translations.literal: When they reached West River the bandits pressed close in pursuit; they went ashore and ran to the Wei family stockade.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached West River the bandits pressed close in pursuit. They went ashore and ran to the Wei family stockade.

sentences.zh: 夫婦要同死，氏訣凝禧曰：「同死固甘，但君尚無子，老母在堂，幸速逃，明早可於此地尋我。
