translations.literal: This is the Zhang family's single thread—nurture him well.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Zhang family's lone heir—raise him well.

sentences.zh: 」言訖，挺身跳洞外，洞高數十仞，亂石巉巖若鋒刃，碎身死焉。

translations.literal: " When she had spoken, she threw herself straight out of the cave; the cave was dozens of ren high, jumbled rocks steep as blade edges, and she died with her body shattered.
translations.idiomatic: " With that she leapt straight from the cave. It was dozens of ren high, its rocks jagged as blades, and she was dashed to pieces.

sentences.zh: 方氏，桐城錢秉鐙妻。

translations.literal: Lady Fang, wife of Qian Bingdeng of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fang, wife of Qian Bingdeng of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 避寇寓南都。

translations.literal: Fleeing bandits she lodged in the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing the turmoil she took refuge in the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 歲祎，饘粥不給，以女紅易米食其夫，己與婢仆雜食糠乞。

translations.literal: In the yi year, porridge was not enough; with needlework she exchanged for rice to feed her husband, while she and maidservants mixed chaff with bran for their own food.
translations.idiomatic: In the yi year porridge ran short. She traded her needlework for rice to feed her husband, while she and the servants ate bran mixed with chaff.

sentences.zh: 客過，潔茗治饌，取諸簪珥，與秉鐙遊者，未嘗知其貧也。

translations.literal: When guests passed she prepared clean tea and food, taking from her hairpins and earrings—those who traveled with Bingdeng never knew of her poverty.
translations.idiomatic: When guests called she served them clean tea and a proper meal, drawing on her hairpins and earrings. Those who traveled with Bingdeng never guessed how poor they were.

sentences.zh: 秉鐙與阮大鋮同里，有隙，避吳中。

translations.literal: Bingdeng was from the same district as Ruan Dacheng; they had a rift, and he fled to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Bingdeng was from the same district as Ruan Dacheng. They had a feud, and he fled to the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 方挈子女追尋，得之。

translations.literal: Fang took her children in pursuit and found him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang took the children and went after him until she found him.

sentences.zh: 已而吳中亦亂，方知不免，乃密紉上下服，抱女赴水死。

translations.literal: Before long Wu too was in turmoil; Fang knew she could not escape; she secretly sewed together her upper and lower garments, embraced her daughter, and went into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Wu region too fell into chaos. Knowing she could not escape, Fang secretly stitched her upper and lower garments together, held her daughter, and drowned them both.

sentences.zh: 陸氏，嘉定黃應爵妻。

translations.literal: Lady Lu, wife of Huang Yingjue of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu, wife of Huang Yingjue of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 少喪夫，家貧，紡績自給逾三十年。

translations.literal: She lost her husband young; the family was poor; spinning and weaving supported herself for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: She lost her husband young. The household was poor, and for more than thirty years she supported herself by spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 甫歿，嘉定城破。

translations.literal: He had just died when Jiading's walls were breached.
translations.idiomatic: He had only just died when Jiading's walls were breached.

sentences.zh: 子道弘妻，亡其姓，持二女倉卒欲赴井。

translations.literal: His son Daohong's wife, her surname lost, in haste took her two daughters intending to throw herself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daohong's wife—her surname is not recorded—seized her two daughters in haste and prepared to throw herself into a well.

sentences.zh: 長女曰：「若使母先投，必戀念吾二女，不如先之。

translations.literal: The elder daughter said, "If our mother throws herself in first, she will surely linger in mind over us two daughters—it is better if we go first.
translations.idiomatic: The elder daughter said, "If Mother goes in first she will surely fret over us two girls. Better that we go first.

sentences.zh: 」乃挽妹亟入，道弘妻繼之，並溺死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she pulled her younger sister quickly in; Daohong's wife followed, and all drowned together.
translations.idiomatic: " She pulled her younger sister in at once. Daohong's wife followed, and all three drowned.

sentences.zh: 於氏，丹陽荊潹妻。

translations.literal: Lady Yu, wife of Jing Shan of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu, wife of Jing Shan of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 潹父大澈為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: Shan's father Dache was killed by mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's father Dache was killed by mutinous troops.

sentences.zh: 於聞變，知不免，謂潹曰：「請先殺妾。

translations.literal: Yu heard of the disaster and knew she could not escape; she said to Shan, "Please kill me first.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu heard what had happened she knew she could not escape. She said to Shan, "Kill me first, I beg you.

sentences.zh: 」潹不忍，怒曰：「君不自殺，欲留為亂兵汙耶！

translations.literal: " Shan could not bear it; she angrily said, "If you will not kill yourself, do you mean to stay and be defiled by mutinous soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: " Shan could not bear to do it. Yu cried angrily, "If you will not kill yourself, do you mean to stay and be defiled by the mutineers!

sentences.zh: 」潹慟哭從之。

translations.literal: " Shan wailed and followed her in death.
translations.idiomatic: " Shan wept bitterly and followed her to his death.

sentences.zh: 項淑美，淳安人，適方希文。

translations.literal: Xiang Shumei, a native of Chun'an, had married Fang Xiwen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Shumei of Chun'an had married Fang Xiwen.

sentences.zh: 希文好蓄書。

translations.literal: Xiwen loved to collect books.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwen was an avid collector of books.

sentences.zh: 杭州不守，大帥方國安潰兵掠江滸，數百里無寧宇。

translations.literal: Hangzhou was lost to defense; the Grand Marshal Fang Guo'an's routed troops plundered along the river shores; for several hundred li there was no peaceful dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: When Hangzhou fell, the routed troops of Grand Marshal Fang Guo'an looted the river country for hundreds of li without a peaceful home left standing.

sentences.zh: 希文避山間，載書以往。

translations.literal: Xiwen fled into the mountains, carrying his books as he went.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwen fled into the hills, taking his books with him.

sentences.zh: 會幼子病疹，希文出延醫，淑美與一嫗一婢處。

translations.literal: It happened his young son had measles; Xiwen went out to summon a physician; Shumei remained with one old woman and one maid.
translations.idiomatic: His young son came down with measles, and Xiwen went out to fetch a doctor. Shumei was left with one old woman and one maid.

sentences.zh: 是夕，亂兵突至，縱火肆掠。

translations.literal: That evening mutinous troops burst in and set fires to plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: That evening mutinous soldiers burst in, set fires, and looted at will.

sentences.zh: 婢挽淑美衣，欲與俱出，正色叱曰：「出則死於兵，不出死於火，等死耳，死火不辱。

translations.literal: The maid pulled Shumei's garment wanting to leave together; she sternly rebuked her, saying, "If we go out we die at the soldiers' hands; if we stay we die in the fire—it is death either way; to die by fire is no disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: The maid tugged at Shumei's robe, urging her to flee together. She rebuked her sternly: "Go out and we die by the sword; stay and we die by fire. Death is the same either way, but to die by fire is no disgrace.

sentences.zh: 」時嫗已先去，見火熾復入，呼曰：「火至，奈何弗出？

translations.literal: " By then the old woman had already left first; seeing the flames fierce she came back in and called, "The fire has come—why do you not go out?
translations.idiomatic: " The old woman had already fled, but seeing the blaze she returned and cried, "The fire is here—why will you not come out?

sentences.zh: 」淑美不應，急取書霍左右，高與身等，坐其中。

translations.literal: " Shumei did not answer; hastily she gathered books and piled them on all sides as high as her body, and sat within them.
translations.idiomatic: " Shumei did not reply. She hurriedly heaped books around her until they stood as high as she was, and sat within the pile.

sentences.zh: 須臾火迫，書盡焚，遂死。

translations.literal: In a moment the fire pressed close; the books were all burned, and she died.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment the flames closed in. The books burned away and she perished.

sentences.zh: 賊退，希文歸，則余燼旋而成堆，若護其骨者。

translations.literal: The bandits withdrew; Xiwen returned, and the remaining embers had already formed into a heap as if protecting her bones.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew and Xiwen returned, the embers had already settled into a heap as though shielding her bones.

sentences.zh: 一慟，灰即散，乃收骨瘞先兆。

translations.literal: At one burst of grief the ashes scattered; he then gathered her bones and buried them by her former grave mound.
translations.idiomatic: At a single sob of grief the ashes scattered. He gathered her bones and buried them beside her husband's grave.

sentences.zh: 先是，有慈谿王氏，歸同里方姓。

translations.literal: Before this there was Lady Wang of Cixi, who had married a man surnamed Fang of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there was Lady Wang of Cixi, who had married a Fang clansman of the same district.

sentences.zh: 甫逾月，火起，延及其屋。

translations.literal: Barely a month had passed when fire broke out and spread to her house.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later fire broke out and spread to her house.

sentences.zh: 夫適他出，氏堅坐小樓不下，遂被焚，骸骨俱燼，惟心獨存。

translations.literal: Her husband happened to be out elsewhere; Lady Wang sat firmly in the small tower and would not come down; she was burned; her bones were all ash, only her heart remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Her husband happened to be away. Lady Wang sat steadfast in the upper room and would not come down. She was consumed in the flames; her bones were ash, but her heart alone remained whole.

sentences.zh: 夫歸，捧之長號，未頃即化。

translations.literal: When her husband returned he held it and wailed long; in no time it turned to dust.
translations.idiomatic: When her husband returned he held it and wailed until it crumbled to dust in his hands.

sentences.zh: 甬上四烈婦。

translations.literal: The Four Fiercely Chaste Wives of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Four Fiercely Chaste Wives of Yong.

sentences.zh: 錢塘張氏，鄞縣舉人楊文瓚妻。

translations.literal: Lady Zhang of Qiantang, wife of Yang Wencan, a presented scholar of Yin county.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang of Qiantang, wife of Yang Wencan, a presented scholar of Yin county.

sentences.zh: 國變後，文瓚與兄文琦，友華夏、屠獻宸，俱坐死。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change Wencan, his elder brother Wenqi, their friends Hua Xia and Tu Xianchen, all were implicated and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic change Wencan, his elder brother Wenqi, and their friends Hua Xia and Tu Xianchen were all implicated and executed.

sentences.zh: 張紉箴聯其首，棺殮畢，即盛服題絕命詩，遍拜族戚。

translations.literal: Zhang gathered their heads with needles and thread, and when coffining and encoffining were complete, immediately donned full dress, composed a death-poem, and paid respects throughout to kinsmen and affines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sewed their severed heads back in place. When the coffining was finished she dressed in her finest garments, wrote a farewell poem, and bowed to every kinsman and relation.

sentences.zh: 吞腦子不死，以佩帶自縊而卒。

translations.literal: She swallowed crushed gelsemium seeds but did not die; with her belt she hanged herself and expired.
translations.idiomatic: She swallowed gelsemium but did not die, then hanged herself with her belt and expired.

sentences.zh: 文琦妻沈氏亦自縊。

translations.literal: Wenqi's wife Lady Shen also hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Wenqi's wife Lady Shen hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 夏繼妻陸氏結帨於梁，引頸就縊，身肥重，帨絕墮地。

translations.literal: Xia Ji's wife Lady Lu tied a kerchief on the beam, drew her neck to hang herself; her body was fat and heavy—the kerchief broke and she fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Ji's wife Lady Lu tied a scarf to the beam and put her neck into the noose, but her body was heavy and the scarf snapped, dropping her to the floor.

sentences.zh: 時炎暑，流汗沾衣，乃坐而搖扇，謂其人曰：「余且一涼。

translations.literal: It was sweltering summer; sweat soaked her garments; she sat and fanned herself, saying to those present, "I must cool off a little first.
translations.idiomatic: It was midsummer and sweat drenched her clothes. She sat down and fanned herself, telling the others, "Let me cool off a moment first.

sentences.zh: 」既復取帨結之而盡。

translations.literal: " Then she took the kerchief again, tied it, and finished the act.
translations.idiomatic: " Then she tied the scarf again and completed the deed.

sentences.zh: 有司聞楊、華三婦之縊，遣丐婦四人至獻宸家，防其妻朱氏甚嚴。

translations.literal: The authorities heard of the three wives Yang and Hua who had hanged themselves and sent four beggar-women to Xianchen's house to guard his wife Lady Zhu very strictly.
translations.idiomatic: When officials learned that the three wives of the Yang and Hua households had hanged themselves, they sent four beggar-women to Xianchen's house to watch his wife Lady Zhu closely.

sentences.zh: 朱不得間，陽為歡笑以接之，且時時誚三婦之徒自苦也。

translations.literal: Zhu could find no opening; she feigned mirth in receiving them and from time to time mocked the three wives and their kind for tormenting themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu found no chance to act. She greeted them with feigned cheer and often mocked the three wives for making themselves suffer.

sentences.zh: 數日，防者稍懈，因謂之曰：「我將一浴，汝儕可暫屏。

translations.literal: After several days the guards relaxed slightly; she therefore said to them, "I am going to bathe—you can withdraw for a while.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the watch grew lax. She told them, "I am going to bathe—you may step outside for a while.

sentences.zh: 」丐婦聽之，闔戶自盡。

translations.literal: " The beggar-women complied; she shut the door and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: " The beggar-women agreed. She shut the door and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 時稱「甬上四烈婦。」

translations.literal: At the time they were called "The Four Fiercely Chaste Wives of Yong."
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were called "The Four Fiercely Chaste Wives of Yong."

sentences.zh: 夏氏，黔國公沐天波侍女也。

translations.literal: Lady Xia was a waiting-woman of Mu Tianbo, Duke of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia was a waiting-woman in the household of Mu Tianbo, Duke of Qian.

sentences.zh: 沙定州之亂，天波出走，母陳、妻焦亦避外舍。

translations.literal: During the disorders in Shading Prefecture, Tianbo fled; his mother Chen and wife Jiao also took refuge in an outer lodge.
translations.idiomatic: During the uprising in Shading Prefecture, Tianbo fled. His mother Chen and his wife Jiao took refuge in an outlying lodge.

sentences.zh: 懼賊迫，焦謂姑曰：「吾輩皆命婦，可陷賊手乎！

translations.literal: Fearing the bandits would press close, Jiao said to her mother-in-law, "We are all wives bound by fate—can we fall into the bandits' hands!
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the rebels would close in, Jiao said to her mother-in-law, "We are all wives of rank—can we fall into the enemy's hands?

sentences.zh: 」舉火自焚死。

translations.literal: " They set fire and burned themselves to death.
translations.idiomatic: " They set a fire and burned themselves to death.

sentences.zh: 夏歸其母家，獲免。

translations.literal: Xia returned to her mother's family and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Xia returned to her mother's home and escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 後天波自永昌還，夏復歸府，則已為尼矣。

translations.literal: Later when Tianbo returned from Yongchang, Xia returned to the mansion—she had already become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Tianbo returned from Yongchang, Xia came back to the household, but she had already taken vows as a nun.

sentences.zh: 天波感其義，俾佐內政。

translations.literal: Tianbo was moved by her righteousness and had her assist in domestic governance.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbo was moved by her integrity and had her help manage the inner household.

sentences.zh: 及天波從亡緬甸，夏遂自經。

translations.literal: When Tianbo followed the flight into Burma, Xia then hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianbo followed the court into exile in Burma, Xia hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 時城中大亂，死者載道，屍為烏犬所食，血肉狼籍，夏屍棄十余日，獨無犯者。

translations.literal: At that time the city was in great turmoil; the dead filled the roads; corpses were eaten by crows and dogs; flesh and blood lay in heaps—Xia's corpse was cast aside for more than ten days, yet none violated it.
translations.idiomatic: The city was then in chaos; the dead choked the streets and crows and dogs fed on the corpses until flesh and blood littered the ground. Xia's body lay abandoned for more than ten days, yet no one touched it.
